text:
Cobrin c. McGill University

2025 QCCS 5198

SUPERIOR COURT

(Class
Actions)

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

Montreal

No.:

500-06-001375-258

DATE:

December 22, 2025

_____________________________________________________________________

BY
THE HONOURABLE dominique poulin, j.s.c.

_____________________________________________________________________

DAVID COBRIN

Applicant

v.

MCGILL UNIVERSITY

Respondent

_____________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT

(Application for LEAVE TO
ADDUCE RELEVANT EVIDENCE)

_____________________________________________________________________

OVERVIEW

[
1
]

The relevant facts of the matter were summarized
by the Court in a prior judgment.
[1]

[
2
]

Briefly, the Applicant seeks authorization to
institute a class action against McGill University (“
McGill
”) on behalf
of McGill’s Jewish students, for damages they suffered during a series of
protests which took place on McGill’s campus after the events of October 7,
2023, in relation to the international conflict between Israel and Palestine.

[
3
]

The Applicant alleges that the protestors
engaged in antisemitic and anti-Zionist activities and speeches, which resulted
in discrimination against class members. He further alleges that the proposed
class members were harassed, were prevented from attending their classes and
that certain were even assaulted, the whole in violation of the
Quebec
Charter
[2]

and the McGill Policies.

[
4
]

McGill is blamed for failing to take meaningful
and expeditious disciplinary actions against the perpetrators, allowing the
activities to continue and intensify.

[
5
]

The Respondent, McGill, requests leave to adduce
appropriate evidence in anticipation of the hearing of the Application for
Authorization of the Applicant.

[
6
]

McGill argues that the proposed evidence is
necessary
to contextualize and
complete the Applicant’s allegations and exhibits
and to
enlighten the Court in its analysis of the criteria of article 575 of the
Code
of Civil Procedure
.

[
7
]

More particularly, McGill requests to submit
evidence of multiple court proceedings which it has taken to address the issue raised
by the Applicant. It requests permission to file proceedings and exhibits
underlying the judgments which were rendered in the course of injunction
proceedings which it initiated or supported. McGill also requests permission to
submit evidence of proceedings filed in the course of a public arbitration
involving the Quebec Public Interest Research Group at McGill (“
QPIRG
”),
after McGill notified this organization to cease supporting Students for Palestine’s Honour and Resistance at McGill” (“
SPHR
”)
as one of its working groups.

[
8
]

The Applicant leaves McGill’s application to the
discretion of the Court.

DISCUSSION

[
9
]

The evidence proposed
by McGill is brought to clarify and complete factual elements which are
essential to the Application.
[3]
They are directly linked to the
allegations raised against McGill and allow the Court to obtain a full picture
of McGill’s intervention. At the present stage, it appears that the Applicant
has filed only partial evidence of McGill’s proceedings in relation to the
protests.

[
10
]

Given its nature,
the evidence is
not be susceptible of being challenged
as to its scope or probative value, and it does not open a debate as to its
sufficiency.
[4]
The documents are public and constitute proceedings and evidence
filed by McGill. They are not filed to make evidence of the veracity of the
contents, but to demonstrate what position has been taken by McGill and the context
of its interventions.

[
11
]

To this extent, the Court allows the evidence to
be adduced.

FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT
:

[
12
]

GRANTS

the Application to adduce appropriate evidence at
the authorization

hearing;

[
13
]

AUTHORIZES

the Respondent, McGill University, to file Exhibits
R-1 to R-10;

[
14
]

THE
WHOLE
without costs.

__________________________________

DOMINIQUE POULIN, J.S.C.

Upon review of the file
